name: Auto workshops and service centres

problems.words: Customer approved one amount, the final bill is higher, then a fight
quick_ideas: Put every estimate in writing before work starts, so there's something to point to
Get the customer's written okay for any extra work, so surprises are agreed first.

workzap_build.text: a digital job card where the estimate and any extra work go to the customer on WhatsApp for a one-reply approval, logged on the job every time.

problems.ask_first: Is the estimate written today, or given verbally?
problems.free_stops: The approval flow and job card layout are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count this week's jobs where the final bill changed after approval, so you see how often surprise extras are starting arguments.
Keep one written extras list at the front desk under one person's watch, so added work gets agreed before the bill grows.

problems.words: Cars sit for days because parts haven't come
quick_ideas: List every car waiting for a part with the supplier and promised date, so you know who to chase
Tell the customer the expected date as soon as you have it, so they hear it from you.

workzap_build.text: a parts request tracker showing supplier, expected date and car waiting, with overdue alerts.

problems.ask_first: Is it mostly one or two suppliers who are late, or parts of every kind arriving slowly?
problems.free_stops: Supplier records and alert rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each waiting car, promised part date and actual arrival in one page this week, so delay patterns by supplier become visible.
Give one person the waiting-parts board and customer update call at the same time daily, so parked cars get chased consistently.

problems.words: Same car comes back next week with the same problem
quick_ideas: Link each comeback to its original job, so patterns show
Talk through the week's comebacks with the team once, so causes are discussed, not argued.

workzap_build.text: a comeback log tied to the original job card, showing patterns by job type and mechanic over time.

problems.ask_first: Does the same fault come back mostly on one type of job, or across all kinds of repairs?
problems.free_stops: How comebacks are classified and reviewed is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count this week's comeback jobs by original repair type, so you can spot where repeat work is eating bay time.
Assign one person to review every comeback with the original job card before new work starts, so repeat issues are handled with context.

problems.words: I don't know which mechanic is productive and which is sitting
quick_ideas: Note on each job card who did it and when it started and finished, so work can be counted
Total jobs per mechanic at the end of the week, so you have a first picture.

workzap_build.text: a bay board and mechanic view of jobs done, hours booked and comebacks, updated every day.

problems.ask_first: Is the idle time mostly on certain days, or does it vary between mechanics all week?
problems.free_stops: The measures used and how they're shown are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each mechanic's started jobs against finished jobs this week, so idle time and handover delays show up clearly.
Make one person update a single bay board whenever a job moves stage, so workload stops being guessed by who looks busy.

problems.words: Parts are taken from stock and never billed
quick_ideas: Issue parts only against a job card, so every part has a home
Count your fast-moving parts and oils once this week, so you know the starting gap.

workzap_build.text: a parts register where every issue is tied to a job so it reaches the bill, with low-stock alerts.

problems.ask_first: Do the missing parts mostly come from fast-moving items like oil and filters, or from costly spares?
problems.free_stops: Issue rules and count routines are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this week's billed parts against parts taken to open jobs, so you can see where stock leaves without sales.
Give one storekeeper the only stock issue notebook beside the parts shelf, so every part taken gets tied to a job.

problems.words: Customers keep calling to ask if the car is ready
quick_ideas: Give a promised time at check-in, so the customer knows when to expect it
Let the customer know the moment it's ready, so they don't need to call.

workzap_build.text: "car ready" and delay messages sent from the job card to the customer, with their permission.

problems.ask_first: Do most calls come in the afternoon, or all day long whenever a car is due?
problems.free_stops: Message timing and triggers are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many ready-status calls come in before noon each day, so you see when silence from the workshop is driving interruptions.
Set one fixed update time daily for all waiting cars under one staff member, so incoming calls stop breaking the front desk flow.

problems.words: Fleet companies pay very late and cash is stuck
quick_ideas: List each fleet client's open invoices by age, so you know who to chase first
Agree one payments contact at each client, so chasing goes to the right person.

workzap_build.text: a ledger for fleet and insurance accounts with ageing alerts and statements sent to clients every month.

problems.ask_first: Is it a few large fleet clients holding most of the money, or many smaller ones?
problems.free_stops: Statement timing and reminder steps are in the solution document; credit terms are for your accountant.

extra_ideas.text: Compare open fleet invoices by company and by oldest month this week, so you can see which accounts are blocking cash longest.
Give one staff member one notebook for all fleet follow-ups every afternoon, so collection chasing happens regularly without scattered notes.

problems.words: No damage photos before work, then the customer says we scratched it
quick_ideas: Photograph every car at check-in, so its condition is on record
Make that reception's job, so it doesn't depend on a busy mechanic.

workzap_build.text: check-in photos on phone saved against each job card with a time stamp, every car, every time.

problems.ask_first: Does it occur mostly on busy days, or whenever reception hands the car straight to a mechanic?
problems.free_stops: The photo routine and storage are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count this week's check-ins with no arrival photos before work begins, so you know how often missing proof is feeding scratch disputes.
Make reception own one arrival condition log for every vehicle at handover, so photo proof gets captured before the keys move inside.

problems.words: Cash at the counter is less than the jobs done
quick_ideas: Number job cards and bills in sequence, so a missing one stands out
Count cash against closed jobs at closing, so gaps show the same day.

workzap_build.text: a daily cash-up matching payments to closed jobs, sent to the owner each evening.

problems.ask_first: Is the shortfall mostly on certain days, or does it show a little every day?
problems.free_stops: The cash-up steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare today's closed job cards with today's cash and billed amounts at closing, so the shortfall is narrowed to the same day.
Give one person the closing cash check and one notebook for differences, so missing money is flagged before the next shift starts.

problems.words: Customers forget us after the oil change
quick_ideas: Tell customers their next service date at pickup, so they leave with a reason to return
Ask permission to remind them, so you can reach out before AC or tyre season.

workzap_build.text: next-service reminders with booking slots, sent directly to customers.

problems.ask_first: Do most customers return for something else eventually, or do they go to a different garage?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and booking setup are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark this week's oil change customers in one notebook, so you can see how many past visits never turned into another booking.
Give one staff member a daily callback list for past oil change customers, so your workshop stays top of mind between services.

never_say: Any diagnosis, or that a car is safe to drive; refer to a qualified technician, and emergency services if anyone is hurt.
Advice on waste oil, coolant, acid or paint disposal rules.
Insurance claim advice, or help inflating claims, faking invoices or tampering with emissions or odometers.
Labour law, wages or apprentice-age advice.
Covert surveillance of staff or naming individuals as thieves.
Storing customer plates with names or phone numbers.

sample_reply.person: Estimate aur final bill ka jhagra roz hota hai, koi solution do.
sample_reply.pi:
Ji haan, ye theek ho sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, kaam shuru hone se pehle har estimate likh kar dein, taake dono ke paas ek hi raqam ho.
Doosra, extra kaam ke liye pehle customer ki likhit haan lein, taake bill pe koi hairani na ho.
Workzap is ke liye ye bana sakta hai: digital job card jis se estimate aur extra kaam customer ko WhatsApp pe approval ke liye khud jaye.
